content.text: I reviewed this item against the five criteria and found no defects.

input.summary: The item passes all five criteria. A rightward SRAS shift is a positive supply shock, so the SRPC shifts down and left and inflation and unemployment both fall. Only option B is correct.
input.scope_skill_notes: The item is on topic 5.2 and links an AD-AS supply shock to a shift of the SRPC. The student has to connect the two models, which fits skill 2.B.
input.key_scoring_notes: Option B is the only defensible answer. Option C describes an AD increase. Option E describes a negative supply shock. Options A and D are wrong on the LRPC and on the claim that nothing shifts.
input.stimulus_expression_notes: No stimulus is needed. The stem is clear and uses standard AP terms. The five options follow the A-E format.
input.distractor_explanation_notes: Each distractor targets a distinct misconception: the natural rate changing, movement along the curve instead of a shift, no effect without an AD shift, and the direction of the shock reversed. The explanation addresses every wrong option.
input.exam_suitability_notes: The item can be answered in about 60 seconds with no calculation, which is typical of the AP exam. Calculator is marked allowed, which is harmless here.
